body:
Its not a bug, it is a core difference between a convex and concave shape in most game physics engines.

A convex shape is an "enclosed volume" test. It is a convex shape of planes that all point reliably inside, easy to test and verify.

A concave shape is not, it is a triangle test. Triangles can point anywhere, testing them for "volume" is horrendously unreliable and bad for performance, hence why it is not done. Such a shape is hollow in both 2D and 3D. A concave shape does not care about its "inside" only when shapes actually touch triangles (or line segments in 2D) they are detected.

That is why you see concave shapes mostly used with hard surface objects like heightmaps or thick level wall geometry that does not move while everything else, from characters to more complex objects, is build with (multiple) convex shapes.

The documentation of the shape type makes this also clear:

> However, ConcavePolygonShape3D is hollow even if the interconnected triangles do enclose a volume, which often makes it unsuitable for physics or detection.

Thanks.
Based on your explanation and reading the documentation and some tests:
- It seems using a smaller shape for ShapeCast3D and sweeping space is more reliable than using a big shape and setting target_position to Vector3.Zero.
- Enabling backface_collision on a Concave collision shape makes it more reliable for collision detection in shape casting.

Maybe someone find these useful later.
